turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Gladys, come through. How are you keeping these days?

[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ag, doctor, not so lekker, if I'm honest. It's that burning when I pass water again, and I've been telling Patience about it since, um, Tuesday, or maybe Monday, the days get mixed up with the loadshedding.
[SEG0003] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She was up and down to the loo all night, doctor. I hardly slept myself.
[SEG0004] person_1 (DOCTOR): Shame. Tell me how it feels, in your own words.

[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): It burns right at the end, like a hot needle when the wee comes out. I go small amounts, again and again, and then I'm back ten minutes later. I even took my library book in, the one about garden birds, because I knew I'd be sitting there.
[SEG0006] person_1 (DOCTOR): Have you had this before?

[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, this is the third time this year. Wait, no, um. January after the family braai, then March at the coast, then June, and actually there was one just after Easter as well, so maybe the fourth.
[SEG0008] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She did phone me about that Easter one. I wasn't staying with her yet then.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): And this time, when did the burning actually start?

[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): I can't put a date on it, doctor, that's the honest truth. Maybe last week after the church bazaar, or the weekend before, I really don't know. I thought at first I'd just held it in too long, because the queue for the ladies was shocking.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any fever, or shivering, or pain in the back under the ribs?

[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever. I checked on the thermometer Patience got at Clicks and it was normal, and I'm not shivering. My back is fine, no pain there at all. It's only low down in the front.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Blood in the urine at all?

[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No blood. I looked, because my neighbour once had blood and she made me promise to always look. The colour is ordinary, just a bit darker first thing in the morning, which I put down to not drinking in the night.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): And on the vaginal side, any discharge, itching, or soreness on the outside?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing like that. I'm not one for those problems, doctor, truly. It's just the urine. I keep myself very clean, front to back, like they taught us.
[SEG0017] person_3 (CAREGIVER): You told me last night it was itchy, Gladys.

[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Ag, Patience, must you say it like that. Well, actually, ja, a little itch on the outside since yesterday, not bad, and I was embarrassed. But there's no discharge, nothing on the liner, I would have seen it.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): That's all right, no need to be shy here. A little itch, and no discharge. Any nausea or vomiting with it?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No vomiting. My tummy was a bit sour, but that was the capsules, and it's settled since I stopped them. I'll explain those, it's a whole story.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm listening.

[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): My sister Lindi, in Durban, she had this same burning in May. When she came up for my birthday she left a strip of capsules in the guest-room drawer, and the box was already in the bin. They're yellow, fairly big, and I don't know the name.
[SEG0023] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I told her to leave them. They'd been sitting there for months, and the writing on the foil was rubbed off.

[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): I know, I know. I took them anyway because I was fed up with the burning and I didn't want to bother you if it was the same old thing. Morning and night, one capsule, for two days. I stopped yesterday morning.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): So four capsules, and you've stopped. Any idea of the milligrams?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Lindi just said they were for her waterworks. I never looked for a number, and now I feel stupid about the whole thing.
[SEG0027] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Could have been anything, doctor. I wouldn't like to guess the name.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Then we won't guess. Please don't take any more of her capsules. What medicines do you take for yourself, regularly?

[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): My sugar tablets, every day, the Glucophage, five hundred milligrams, one with breakfast and one with supper. I've been good with those, Patience watches me. And the water tablet for my pressure, every morning.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): The water tablet. The sister wrote it in your file as hydrochlorothiazide, twelve point five milligrams, once a day.

[SEG0031] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Ag no, doctor, that's not the number. The bottle in the cupboard is twenty-five milligrams, the little white ones. I pop one out for her every morning, so it's twenty-five, not twelve point five.

[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't read the bottle, hey. She puts them in the egg cup with the sugar tablet and I just swallow. I know it's the water one because I wee more afterwards, especially before we walk to the shop.

[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): So the file says twelve point five and the bottle says twenty-five, and we can't settle it sitting here. Bring the bottle next time and we'll correct the notes. The sugar, that's been with you a good while?

[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, diabetes, about eight years, since I retired from the school. I taught grade four at the primary in Scottsville, thirty-one years, can you believe. The pressure they picked up at the same clinic, maybe six years back, and both are still with me.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): And Patience, you stay with her?
[SEG0036] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Mornings every day, and I sleep over three nights a week. Her daughter is in Australia, so it's me and the cat most of the time.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): The cat is no help, by the way. She sleeps on the printer and won't even look at a gecko.
[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ha, useless security. Any other tablets, anything from the chemist?

[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Panado, sometimes, for my knees, not every day. I haven't needed one this week, with all this other nonsense going on. I don't smoke, I never have, and I don't drink, except a sip of sherry at Christmas that I didn't even finish.
[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any allergy to medicines that you know of?
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing. I've had penicillin and the usual ones with no trouble.
[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): Good. I'm just going to feel your tummy, tell me if anything is sore. Soft, and it doesn't hurt when I press low down. No tenderness over the loins either.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): No, that's not sore. It just feels full, like I need the loo again, which is the story of my week.

[SEG0044] person_1 (DOCTOR): All right. This does sound like another bladder infection, the same sort as the other times this year, though I don't want to call it certain until we've checked the urine.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): I thought so. I hope it's not the kidneys, my uncle lost a kidney, but that was stones, years ago, and he lived in Kokstad, completely different.
[SEG0046] person_1 (DOCTOR): I hear you, but nothing today points to the kidneys. I'd like a urine sample sent off, a dip here and then microscopy and culture.
[SEG0047] person_3 (CAREGIVER): We can do the sample now? She last went just before we got in the car, but she can probably go again, she always can.
[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ja, the sister outside will give you a jar just now. It's ordered, we'll send it off today.

[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): Must I start an antibiotic today, or do we wait? The burning is really annoying, I won't lie, especially when I'm trying to watch the news and I have to pause it every five minutes.

[SEG0050] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'd rather not start one today. If we throw another antibiotic in before the sample, we muddy the result. Rather stop Lindi's capsules for good, and drink plenty of water, and we'll see what grows.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): Water I can do. I've been trying, though I forget when I'm reading. Patience, you'll nag me, won't you.
[SEG0052] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I already do. She drinks tea all day and counts it as water, doctor.
[SEG0053] person_1 (DOCTOR): Tea is fine, but plain water as well, a glass every hour or so while you're awake. And no more leftover antibiotics, not from Lindi, not from anyone.
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, I promise. I felt so embarrassed buying nothing and just using hers, like I was being sneaky. Even the pharmacist at Dis-Chem knows my face.
[SEG0055] person_1 (DOCTOR): You did the right thing coming in. Come back in a week and we'll go through the result together, whether it's grown something or not.
[SEG0056] person_2 (PATIENT): A week. What if it gets worse before then, the burning, or I start shivering?
[SEG0057] person_1 (DOCTOR): If you get fever, vomiting, or pain in the back, don't wait the week, come straight in or go to the emergency unit. Otherwise I'll see you in a week.
[SEG0058] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I'll bring the water-tablet bottle with us next time, so you can see the twenty-five.
[SEG0059] person_1 (DOCTOR): Perfect, that would help. And Gladys, if the itch on the outside gets worse, mention it when you come, but I'm not going to examine inside today.

[SEG0060] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you, doctor. I was worried you'd want all of that and I didn't even shave, well, you know. We'll be here next week, traffic willing, that robot by the bridge has been out again.
[SEG0061] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sharp. Go past the sister for the jar on your way out, and we'll take it from there.
